new.s: The Chambal ravines, India's classic badland topography, are located in which part of India?
new.x: The Chambal ravines of central India are the best-known badlands of India, formed by a dense gully network.

new.s: Konaseema in Andhra Pradesh is the delta of which river?
new.x: The Godavari delta is called Konaseema; together with the Krishna delta it builds the AP coastal plain.
new.angle: U0601 notes gap: AP delta -> river (Konaseema)

new.s: Which river has carved the Gandikota canyon, known as the 'Grand Canyon of India'?
new.x: The Gandikota canyon in Andhra Pradesh is cut by the Pennar (Penna) River.

new.s: Which river carved the Grand Canyon in Arizona, USA?
new.x: The Grand Canyon, about 446 km long and over 1.8 km deep, was carved by the Colorado River.

new.s: What is the wet, marshy belt south of the Bhabar, where the underground streams re-emerge, called?
new.x: South of the Bhabar the water that vanished underground comes up again, forming the marshy Terai belt.

new.s: At which Prayag does the Mandakini join the Alaknanda?
new.x: Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Mandakini with the Alaknanda; Karnaprayag is for the Pindar.

new.s: Which is the main agent of coastal erosion?
new.x: Waves do most coastal erosion; tides, currents and tsunamis help, but waves are the main agent.
new.angle: U0602 #5/#14 Agent of most coastal erosion

new.s:
Consider the following statements about coastal erosion:
1. Waves are the main agent of coastal erosion.
2. Saltation is one of the processes of coastal erosion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Waves are the main agent; coastal erosion works by hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution. Saltation is a wind process.
new.angle: U0602 #5 Coastal erosion agents and processes

new.s: The term 'karst' comes from the Karst region of which country?
new.x: Karst topography is named after the limestone Karst region of Slovenia.
new.angle: U0602 notes gap: karst -> name origin

new.s: Which cave of Andhra Pradesh was declared a GSI Geo-Heritage Site in June 2025?
new.x: Belum Caves in Nandyal, India's second-longest cave, were declared a GSI Geo-Heritage Site in June 2025.

new.s: Exfoliation is an example of which type of weathering?
new.x: Exfoliation breaks rock without any chemical change, so it is physical weathering.

new.s: What are the lava-capped mesas of central India called?
new.x: The Patland of central India consists of lava-capped mesas.
new.angle: U0602 PYQ y9762878cb24 angle (regional term) other way round

new.s: Which is the third most abundant gas in dry air by volume?
new.x: Dry air is nitrogen (78%) > oxygen (21%) > argon (0.93%) > carbon dioxide (0.04%).
new.angle: U0603 PYQ y4b6103a7175 gases ranked by volume

new.s: Which of the following is the most abundant greenhouse gas in the atmosphere?
new.x: Water vapour (0-4%) is the most abundant greenhouse gas; it absorbs most infrared in the lower atmosphere.

new.s: Which elements released by halocarbons destroy ozone in the stratosphere?
new.x: Halocarbons such as CFCs and halons release chlorine and bromine, which break down ozone.
new.angle: U0603 #9 Ozone-depleting substances (APPSC PYQ halocarbons angle)

new.s: Who among the following first reported the Antarctic ozone hole in 1985?
new.x: The Antarctic ozone hole was reported in 1985 by the British team of Farman, Gardiner and Shanklin.

new.s: Which clouds help the formation of the Antarctic ozone hole?
new.x: Polar stratospheric clouds in the Antarctic spring (Aug-Nov) speed up ozone loss.

new.s: What does the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol phase down?
new.x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) phases down HFCs by 80-85%; HFCs spare ozone but are strong warming gases.

new.s: Which of the following are the first universally ratified treaties in UN history?
new.x: The Vienna Convention (1985) and the Montreal Protocol (1987) were the first UN treaties ratified by all countries.

new.s: By which name is the F layer of the ionosphere also known?
new.x: The F layer is the Appleton layer and is the main reflector of short-wave radio; the E layer is Kennelly-Heaviside.

new.s: According to the India Meteorological Department, what is the minimum maximum-temperature threshold for a heat wave in the plains?
new.x: IMD considers a heat wave in the plains only when the maximum is at least 40°C (37°C on the coast, 30°C in the hills).
new.angle: U0604 #13 IMD heat wave criteria - plains

new.s: Which of the following districts was listed as a severe-heatwave district in Andhra Pradesh's Heat Action Plan 2026?
new.x: Palnadu, with Tirupati, Prakasam, SPSR Nellore, Markapuram, Guntur and Bapatla, was a severe-heatwave district in HAP 2026.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about IMD criteria:
1. A heat wave in coastal areas needs a maximum temperature of at least 37°C.
2. A cold wave in the plains needs a minimum temperature of 10°C or below.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: IMD uses 37°C as the coastal heat-wave threshold and 10°C or below as the cold-wave minimum for the plains.
new.angle: U0604 #13 IMD heat and cold wave criteria

new.s: Where was the world's highest temperature of 56.7°C recorded?
new.x: Death Valley holds the world record of 56.7°C; Vostok holds the coldest (-89.2°C).

new.s: Which January isotherm divides India into tropical and sub-tropical parts?
new.x: The January 18°C isotherm separates tropical south India from sub-tropical north India.

new.s: Which greenhouse gas is known as 'marsh gas'?
new.x: Methane, called marsh gas, comes from paddy fields, wetlands and livestock and gives about 20% of the greenhouse effect.

new.s: What does a sudden fall in the barometer reading generally indicate?
new.x: A sudden fall in pressure means a low is coming, bringing cloud, rain and storm; a rising barometer means fair weather.

new.s: What are lines joining places of equal atmospheric pressure, reduced to sea level, called?
new.x: Isobars join places of equal pressure; closely spaced isobars show a steep pressure gradient and strong winds.

new.s:

new.s: What are the pre-monsoon showers of Kerala and Karnataka known as?
new.x: Pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and Karnataka are called mango showers; Kaal Baisakhi are the storms of Bengal and Assam.
new.angle: U0605 PYQ y26de766d3d3 angle (mango showers) other way round

new.s: Which of the following are rain-bearing clouds?
new.x: 'Nimbus' means rain-bearing; nimbostratus gives steady rain and cumulonimbus gives thunderstorms and hail.

new.s: Through which clouds does the sun appear as if seen through ground glass?
new.x: Altostratus is a grey-blue middle-level sheet through which the sun looks as if seen through ground glass.

new.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh lies in the rain-shadow area?
new.x: Rayalaseema lies on the leeward side of the Western Ghats and so receives scanty rain.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rainfall in peninsular India decreases from west to east.
2. The eastern side of the Western Ghats lies on the leeward side.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Western Ghats force orographic rain on the west; the leeward east side is dry, so rainfall falls from west to east.
new.angle: U0606 #3/#6 Orographic rain and rain shadow

new.s:
